claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: In `src/sqllens/ui/memory_admin.html` (lines 628-641), a memory whose payload has no `groups` key at all is rendered as `untagged`, with the hover text "No groups: every rule set can read it." The guard in `renderGroups` is `groups === null || (groups !== undefined && !Array.isArray(groups))`, so `undefined` deliberately falls past the "unreadable" branch into the "untagged" branch, and `groupKind` classifies it the same way, so the row is also matched by the `untagged` filter choice. The same path is reachable through the row-detail modal: `const m = res.data || {}` at line 956 means a `get_memory` reply that is not an error but carries no body renders a modal whose only row reads `groups: untagged` with that hover text. Today the server always sends the field (`_record_to_wire` in `src/sqllens/memory/admin.py`), so no live path produces it, but the widget is asserting an access fact it has no evidence for, which is the shape AGENTS.md's "failures must surface as structured signal, never as a silent success" rule exists to prevent. Treating an absent key like a non-array value — the `⚠ unreadable` state — would close it. (raised by 1/5 agents)

claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: In `src/sqllens/ui/memory_admin.html` (lines 670-714), the group checklist is hard to use from the keyboard and does not announce its state. The `clear` control is a bare `<a>` with no `href`, `role` or `tabindex`, so it cannot be focused or activated by keyboard. Every checkbox change calls `groupSelChanged()`, which clears and rebuilds the whole menu (`groupMenu.textContent = ""`, line 673), destroying the input the user just toggled, so focus falls back to `<body>` after each toggle. The button carries `aria-haspopup="true"` but `aria-expanded` is never updated, the container uses `role="menu"` while its children are plain checkbox labels rather than `menuitemcheckbox`, and `Escape` does not close the menu. prior_evidence: The prior finding still holds at head. tests/unit/test_memory_admin_widget_render.py:96-211 is one `(async () => {...})()` block with no try/catch. The `<pre id="probe">` is created only at lines 207-210, after every step. Any throw part-way, such as `lab` undefined in clickChoice/clickName (lines 85-95), leaves it unwritten. `_render` (lines 235-236) then fails with `assert match, proc.stderr[-2000:]`. That happens inside the module-scoped `renders` fixture (lines 247-250), so every test using it errors together with a Chromium stderr dump instead of at the behaviour that broke. The steps are also order-dependent: lines 151-166 toggle choices on and off, and later steps such as 169 and 197 assume the earlier toggles left the filter state clean. No fix is present. I searched for the readers of this behaviour: the `renders` fixture and its 11 dependent tests (lines 257-347), plus `_render`. All of them consume the single probe output. No try/catch, per-step capture or partial-output path exists in the file. I did not apply 'No defect' because failures do surface with poor diagnostics: the cost is debuggability and it is not bounded by the inputs. criteria.json (22 criteria, read and valid) has no criterion requiring this structure. Criterion 22 only requires the render test to pass and cover the listed states. The impact is limited to test diagnosability.
